theme: Production readiness of a small ASP.NET Core parcel-tracking service (API + polling worker + EF Core/PostgreSQL + two upstream HTTP services): almost ready, with realistic gaps

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The merchant-webhook HttpClient is registered with a base address only: no resilience handler, no retry, no circuit breaker and no explicit timeout (the 100 s HttpClient default applies to every attempt). One slow merchant endpoint holds the notification worker for 100 s per parcel, and a merchant that is down is hammered on every poll. The carrier client in the same file shows the team knows the standard resilience handler (TRP-003).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: FindByTrackingNumberAsync accepts a CancellationToken and does not forward it to the EF Core query, so an aborted HTTP request (or a stopping host) still waits for the database round trip. Every other store method forwards its token.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The polling BackgroundService has no graceful shutdown: ExecuteAsync loops on while (true) and never reads its stoppingToken, the delay between polls takes no token, and the PollOnceAsync helper it calls accepts no token at all, so carrier and database calls run uncancellable. On SIGTERM the host waits out its shutdown timeout and then abandons the loop mid-poll.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The delivery-performance report controller carries no [Authorize] attribute and the application sets no fallback policy, so GET /api/reports/merchants/{merchantId}/delivery-performance returns any merchant's parcel volumes and failure rates to an anonymous caller. Every other controller requires a named policy, and the reports:read policy this endpoint was meant to use is defined but never applied.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The redirect request model carries no validation attributes: PickupPointId is only implicitly required (non-nullable) and otherwise unconstrained - any length and characters, while its column holds 32 - HoldUntil may lie in the past, and Note is unbounded while its column holds 500. POST /api/parcels/{trackingNumber}/redirect binds it straight into the domain call, so an oversized value surfaces as a database error (HTTP 500) and a past hold date is stored as-is. The shipment registration model beside it is fully annotated.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: ParcelTracking.Worker
entries.rationale: The notification dispatcher reports deliveries and failures with Console.WriteLine / Console.Error.WriteLine instead of the injected ILogger used everywhere else in the worker: the lines bypass log levels, categories, structured properties and the OpenTelemetry log exporter, so webhook failures never reach the log pipeline.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The carrier API health check catches every exception and discards it in an empty catch, then falls through to HealthCheckResult.Healthy(): when the carrier API is unreachable (DNS failure, refused connection, timeout) the readiness endpoint and the worker's heartbeat report Healthy, which is exactly the condition the check exists to report.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The worker calls Database.EnsureCreated() at startup against the same PostgreSQL database the API evolves with versioned EF Core migrations. On an empty database it creates the schema from the current model without the __EFMigrationsHistory table, so the next migrations bundle run fails (tables already exist); the schema is no longer owned by the migration path.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Repository-level CI posture: .github/workflows/ci.yml collects coverage on every run (dotnet test --collect "XPlat Code Coverage") and uploads the Cobertura report as an artifact, but nothing compares it with a threshold, so coverage can fall to zero without failing a build. No other CI gate defect exists (no test filter, no skipped tests, tests run on pull requests).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The /labels branch (shipping-label PDFs, opened by merchants in a browser) is split off with app.Map before the security-headers middleware is added, so label responses carry no Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options or frame policy, while every /api response does.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: HSTS is configured in the service collection (AddHsts with a one-year max-age) but app.UseHsts() is never called, so production responses never send Strict-Transport-Security; only the redirect protects first requests, and nothing in the deployment manifests adds the header either.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A warning is logged with an interpolated string, so the carrier code and HTTP status are baked into the message text instead of being structured properties; every other log call in the repository uses a message template.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: /health/live and /health/ready are anonymous on purpose: the kubelet probes them without credentials, and they return only Healthy/Unhealthy with no data.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: /.well-known/security.txt (RFC 9116) must be readable by anyone: it is the public vulnerability-reporting contact.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The carrier API client is registered with AddStandardResilienceHandler (rate limiter, total timeout, retry with jittered back-off, circuit breaker, per-attempt timeout), tuned from configuration.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The published client library registers its typed HttpClient and returns the IHttpClientBuilder so the consuming application adds the resilience policy that fits it (documented in the XML doc). A library that hard-wired retries would retry non-idempotent calls on behalf of callers it cannot see; leaving the policy to the host is the recommended design.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Stale-while-revalidate: a request that finds the carrier directory stale is answered from the cached copy and starts a background refresh with CancellationToken.None. The comment says why: the refresh must outlive the request that noticed the staleness (the request's token would cancel it as soon as the response is sent); it is bounded by the resilient client's total timeout and its failures are logged inside RefreshAsync.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: ParcelTracking.Cli
entries.rationale: parcel-admin is an interactive command-line tool: its output IS the user interface, written to stdout and errors to stderr with a non-zero exit code. Routing it through ILogger would add timestamps and categories to a report meant for a terminal.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The release workflow builds an EF Core migrations bundle (dotnet ef migrations bundle) from the versioned migrations and attaches it to the release; the deploy workflow runs it before rolling out. This is the versioned migration path, not runtime schema creation.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: EnsureCreated on a throw-away in-memory SQLite database inside the integration-test factory: test fixtures need a schema per test run, not a migration history, and nothing ships this code.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A message template split over two lines with + between two string literals: the compiler folds it into one constant template with named placeholders, so the log call is fully structured.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: An EF Core-generated migration: the tool emits #nullable disable at the top of every migration file. Generated code is outside nullable analysis by design; the projects themselves enable nullable everywhere.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: EF Core-generated migration metadata (// <auto-generated />, #nullable disable).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: EF Core-generated model snapshot (// <auto-generated />, #nullable disable).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: catch (OperationCanceledException) when (stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested) with an empty body: the idiomatic way for a BackgroundService to leave its loop on shutdown. Only the host's own cancellation is caught; any other cancellation propagates.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The image runs only on Kubernetes (ADR 0002, deploy/k8s), which ignores Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK; liveness and readiness are HTTP probes on /health/live and /health/ready in the Deployment. The runtime image has no curl to run a HEALTHCHECK with anyway.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Runs only on Kubernetes; liveness and readiness are exec probes on the worker's heartbeat file, defined in the Deployment.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: ParcelTracking.Client
entries.rationale: A thin published client library over HttpClient: it has nothing of its own to log; IHttpClientFactory already logs every request it sends under the consumer's logging configuration.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The readiness probe's carrier client has an explicit 2-second timeout and deliberately no retry or breaker (the comment says why): a health probe must report the dependency's state now, not what a retry policy eventually achieved; the kubelet's own probe period is the retry.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The outbox dispatcher is safe to re-run: it selects only notifications with DeliveredAt == null whose next attempt is due, marks each delivered after the relay accepts it, and every webhook payload carries the notification's EventId so the relay de-duplicates a resend after a crash between delivery and save. At-least-once delivery with an idempotency key is the designed behaviour. Promoted from a scanner false positive in scan iteration 1.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Repository-level: the one published library, ParcelTracking.Client, exposes five public types (the client, its registration extension and three records) and is versioned by the repository's SemVer <Version> and CHANGELOG. The service's own projects are not published, so the share of public types across the repository says nothing about a library surface. Promoted from a scanner false positive in scan iteration 1.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Repository-level: the awaits without ConfigureAwait(false) are in ASP.NET Core and generic-host application code, which runs without a SynchronizationContext, so there is no context to capture. The one library meant for arbitrary hosts (ParcelTracking.Client) uses ConfigureAwait(false) on every await. Promoted from a scanner false positive in scan iteration 1.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The image comes from the organisation's own registry (ghcr.io/code-assurance-initiative), pinned by digest and built with provenance and SBOM attestations by the release workflow. Which registries a cluster admits is an admission-policy decision of the cluster, not of the workload manifest. Promoted from a scanner false positive in scan iteration 1.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: As TRP-021, for the worker image. Promoted from a scanner false positive in scan iteration 1.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Secrets reach the container as environment variables from secretKeyRef: the standard way to configure an ASP.NET Core application (configuration keys with __), readable only by the unprivileged process itself, with no shell or debug endpoint to leak the environment. Mounting them as files would add a key-per-file configuration provider for no change in exposure. Promoted from a scanner opinion in scan iteration 1 (CKV_K8S_35, umbrella concept: no precise child concept exists).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: As TRP-023, for the worker. Promoted from a scanner opinion in scan iteration 1.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Repository-level: retention is complete - periods documented in docs/operations/data-retention.md and enforced by RetentionSweeper, a scheduled BackgroundService in the worker that purges delivered notifications after 30 days and completed parcels (with history and redirect notes) after 180 days. Promoted from a scanner false positive in scan iteration 2, which still asked for 'a scheduled purge / cleanup job' by name.

entries.label: clean
entries.rationale: Repository-level properties certified clean: every directly referenced NuGet package is the current stable release, supported, non-deprecated, permissively licensed and used by the project that declares it; no package, direct or transitive, has a known vulnerability; the target framework is net10.0; no secret was ever committed; nullable analysis is on in every project (generated EF Core files excepted, TRP-010..012); every CI action is pinned by commit SHA and every base image by digest; Central Package Management plus committed lock files, restored in locked mode in CI.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: ILogger with message templates in the API, infrastructure and most of the worker, OpenTelemetry traces/metrics/logs, health checks with liveness and readiness. Not top of the band: the notification dispatcher writes to the console (RDY-006) and the carrier health check lies (RDY-007).

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: CodeQL on pull requests and pushes, Dependabot for NuGet, Actions and Docker, a vulnerable-package gate in CI. No secret scanner runs in CI (the hosting platform's secret scanning is not in the repository).

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: <Version> 0.4.0 in Directory.Build.props, tag-triggered release workflow, but the CHANGELOG is thin: two versioned entries and a note that earlier history is only in the git log.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: One of the two upstream HTTP clients (carrier API) has the standard resilience pipeline; the other (merchant webhooks, RDY-001) has none. Half-resilient is a middling posture, not a pass.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Versioned EF Core migrations shipped as a bundle and run before each rollout, undermined by the worker's EnsureCreated at startup (RDY-008).

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: ParcelTracking.Client is the one packable library: a small public surface (one client, one registration extension, three records; implementation internal) versioned with the repository's SemVer <Version>.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Reward-leaning: a BenchmarkDotNet project with [MemoryDiagnoser] covers the hot path (carrier status normalisation); it is not run in CI.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: SECURITY.md with private vulnerability reporting, response times and scope; also /.well-known/security.txt served by the API.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Model-judged: SECURITY.md names a private channel, what to include, response times, supported versions and scope. Wide band for judge variance.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Kubernetes Deployments with RollingUpdate (maxUnavailable 0), liveness/readiness probes, PodDisruptionBudgets; a manual deploy workflow behind a protected production environment that runs the migrations bundle first, waits for rollout status and runs kubectl rollout undo on failure.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: docs/operations/backup-and-restore.md: managed PostgreSQL with daily snapshots and point-in-time recovery, RPO 5 min / RTO 1 h, a quarterly restore drill; the services themselves are stateless. Wide band: evidence is documentation, not IaC.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Tests run on every pull request and fail the build, but the coverage that CI collects is never gated (RDY-009).

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: JWT bearer with three named policies on every controller but one: the reports controller is anonymous (RDY-004) and there is no fallback policy to catch it.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: A security-headers middleware covers the API, but the /labels branch is outside it (RDY-010) and no response carries HSTS (RDY-011).

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: UseHttpsRedirection and forwarded headers are configured, HSTS is configured but never applied (RDY-011).
